text:
jessica_cs: Customer Jenny (Acme Corp) reporting 401 invalid_api_key on our private deployment after they rotated keys. They pasted the new key from the console into their app and started seeing failures this morning. Request ID: req_0a3b2c. Can eng take a look?

alan_eng: Can you paste the exact curl and the response body (redact key)? Also any auth-service logs you have for req_0a3b2c.

jessica_cs: Pasting redacted request/response they sent:

```
curl -X POST https://private-us.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Api-Key sk_live_***************" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-rls-1", "input":"hi"}'
```

Response: 401, body: `{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key inactive"}`

Customer also attached an auth-service trace extract (redacted):
```
time=2026-08-11T09:12:03Z level=warn svc=auth-service event=authorize req=req_0a3b2c key_id=key_1802 status=found key_status=disabled reason="pending_ack" subject=org:acme
```

alan_eng: Interesting — the auth-service found the key but key_status=disabled with reason pending_ack. That's not the usual copy-paste newline/trailing-char issue. Did they create the key via the console or API?

jessica_cs: They said they created the key in the Console > API keys for their org and copied it straight into their app. I asked if anyone on their org had to accept any email or prompt — they said no prompt appeared.

alan_eng: For private deployments we added an SSO/org-ack workflow last year: new keys created for org-level scopes are initially in a "pending_ack" state until the org admin confirms the new credential (safety/SLA/legal step for private plans). Usually the console shows a big banner after key creation. Looks like the banner didn't show or they navigated away before confirming. The auth-service will return 401 with invalid_api_key and status details in our logs.

devops_miguel: I can confirm from infra: the key metadata table shows key_1802.created_at=2026-08-11T09:10:58Z, state=pending_ack, creator=jdoe@acme.com. No ack event in audit log.

jessica_cs: Customer says they didn't see any console banner or email. Could we confirm what triggers the ack and whether it should be an email?

alan_eng: Ack is normally a console interaction — button labeled "Confirm new API key" — or via the admin API: POST /orgs/:org_id/keys/:key_id/confirm with admin token. There is also an optional org policy that enforces SSO confirmation by requiring the admin to re-auth via SSO. If the org has that, the key stays disabled until that step completes.

jessica_cs: Ok. I sent the customer the admin-confirm steps and asked them to have their org admin follow them. I also gave them this temp mitigation: reissue a personal-scoped key (not org-scoped) to unblock while they confirm. They asked if we could flip the key active on our side.

alan_eng: We don't flip org-scoped keys active without an explicit ack because of compliance. But we can surface a clearer console CTA and an API error that says "key pending confirmation: visit https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/{org}/keys to confirm" instead of generic invalid_api_key. Filed ENG task.

sre-bot: Deploy notice: UI patch queued to show confirmation banner (patch id: ui-8295), scheduled for next release train.

jessica_cs: Customer followed the admin-confirm API route and confirmed the key at 09:14. After that they retried and got 200. They report no further issues.

alan_eng: Action items: 1) I'll update auth-service to return clearer error code and message for pending_ack (ENG-5821). 2) Docs: CS to add a KB entry describing org-key confirmation flow.

jessica_cs: Thanks — I'll draft KB and send to CS channel for review. :thumbsup:

customer_jdoe: Thanks everyone — confirmed the key and back in business. Appreciate the quick help! :tada:
